paper_metadata.title: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations for financial risk analytics: scenario generation for equity, rate, and credit risk factors

summary: The paper constructs gate‑based quantum circuits that integrate stochastic scenario generation with Quantum Amplitude Estimation for financial risk models (equity binomial trees, Vasicek interest‑rate trinomial trees, and credit risk models). Simulations on a noiseless Qiskit simulator show QAE error scaling δp ∝ 1/N versus classical Monte Carlo δp ∝ 1/√N, but realistic use cases are estimated to require ~1000–1200 qubits and circuit depths up to ~10^8 gates, far beyond current hardware.

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation circuit for equity risk factors using a binomial tree to estimate probabilities such as P(Smax) and P(Smin) as a function of output-qubit count.

algorithm.variant: QAE with phase estimation and Grover-style amplitude amplification
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters fixed from the binomial-tree calibration; no variational initialization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per binomial-tree timestep; |0> and |1> encode down/up moves. Risk measure qubit encodes probability of max/min event via controlled Toffoli/X/Z logic.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate P(Smax)=q^m and P(Smin)=(1-q)^m for the equity price distribution generated by a binomial tree.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Reversible gate construction with ancilla qubits uncomputed after use
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m-2 for Mmax/Mmin (scales linearly with m)

problem_instance.description: Equity price scenario generation for a geometric Brownian motion discretized by a binomial tree; risk measures are maximum and minimum terminal price probabilities.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic binomial-tree parameters; no market dataset

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Quantum circuits assembled for n=1..9 output qubits; results shown with 10,000 shots for output distributions and one-shot convergence plots

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured output z converted to theta and then to p via p=sin^2(z*pi/2^n)

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: monotonic convergence of estimated p toward expected value as n increases

speedup_claims.conditions: fault-tolerant quantum devices; QAE with phase estimation and Grover-style amplitude amplification
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports simulated zero-noise runs and theoretical scaling; no hardware speedup is demonstrated.

speedup_claims.conditions: as output-qubit count increases in QAE
speedup_claims.caveats: The convergence plots are from simulator runs; the asymptotic advantage is theoretical.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/N) estimation error for QAE; circuit depth exponential in n due to repeated Q applications
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(N)) estimation error for Monte Carlo

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; authors only analyze scaling with output qubits n and discuss hypothetical precision requirements (≈14 output qubits for 1 bp error).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Paper estimates realistic financial applications would require ≈1000–1200 input qubits and circuit depth ≲10^8.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only (QAE vs classical Monte Carlo)
Only validated on noiseless classical simulation

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states computations were performed on a classical computer using a zero-noise simulator from Qiskit.
The paper reports m=6 and n=1-9, but does not give a single total qubit count for the full circuit in the experiment section.
Paper explicitly frames the work as theoretical preparation for future fault‑tolerant devices and does not claim practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: End‑to‑end quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation circuit for reduced‑form credit risk, estimating survival probability using a Poisson‑process‑style default model.

algorithm.variant: QAE with phase estimation and Grover-style amplitude amplification

key_results: Survival probability encoded using a sequence of Ry rotations with conditional gates ensuring absorbing default states.
Example parameters: m=6 timesteps, default probability per step q_def ≈ 2%.
Measured probability converges to theoretical value (1 − q_def)^m as output qubits increase (n=1–9).
Histograms produced using 10,000 shots; convergence plots use single-shot estimates.
